Method: I found businesses through WebSearch (standard mode), Superpages/YellowPages category pages pulled with curl (Windsor Mill, Gwynn Oak and Randallstown across child care, martial arts, dance, grooming, PT, pharmacies, home health and tutoring), the detail page for each listing (website field, years in business), MapQuest, Revgear, CareLuLu, 211 Maryland and NPI records. I fetched every candidate website with curl and checked the viewport tag, copyright and dates, site builder, tap-to-call links, forms and booking, meta description and title. I used DNS lookups (dns.google) to confirm when a listed domain no longer exists. No forms were submitted and no business was contacted.

Coverage: 11 of the 12 leads are in 21244 (8) or 21207 (3); one is in 21133.

Caveats:
1. Review counts come from third-party snippets (Google Business, Birdeye, Pawlicy, Revgear, poyst, ClassPass), not from opening Google Maps directly. Confirm on the live Google Business Profile before outreach.
2. MapQuest 'Closed' flags reflect the time the page was captured, not permanent closure.
3. Before pitching, verify childcare licenses with MSDE's Office of Child Care and home-care licenses with Maryland OHCQ.
4. Health-related demo sites should not collect medical information in contact forms unless the client has HIPAA-compliant handling. Use contact-only forms or embed the provider's existing patient portal.
5. Most independent dentists and PT clinics in 21244 already have vendor sites (Officite, TeleVox, Elementor), so they are weaker demo targets than childcare, home care, martial arts and grooming.
6. Two phone checks could add strong 'broken website' leads: Maryland STEM Program and Kenpo Tigers. Both have lapsed domains but unconfirmed operating status.

- Child Care of Windsor's YellowPages/Superpages listing sends visitors to an Illinois car dealership.

I delivered 12 leads, ranked by score. 11 of the 12 are in the target ZIPs: 7 in 21244 and 4 in 21207. The other one, Class Act Catering, is in 21133. Every website verdict comes from fetching the site on 2026-11-09, mostly with curl and an HTML checklist (viewport, copyright, builder fingerprints, forms, tel: links, HTTPS). I used WebFetch where a site blocked plain curl.

Things to know before building demos:

(1) The web search budget for this run (200 calls, shared across agents) ran out partway through. Florists, photographers, DJs, bakeries, food trucks and party rentals are therefore under-represented. The ones I did find had decent sites, could not be verified as operating, or listed home addresses. A follow-up pass on those categories, plus the second-tier barbershops named in the excluded list, would fill the gap.

(2) Two websites were behind bot-protection pages and I did not try to get around them: dennisbevents.com, the site linked from The Ballroom at 1808's listing, and the HTTPS version of windsorinncrabhouse.com. The Ballroom's gap score is conservative for that reason.

(3) The listed website for Windsor Inn, thewindsorbar.com, did not resolve. WebFetch's error notes that a host can also fail this way if the session's network settings block it. A quick check in a normal browser would confirm the domain is truly dead.

(4) Several phone numbers conflict across directories: La Taina, Corinthian, and Windsor Inn's carry-out vs dining-room lines. Corinthian's MenuPages entry says 'Restaurant closed', so confirm by phone or a drive-by before investing in a demo.

(5) Lavish Loft Salon and the Dominican Barbershop are inside Security Square Mall. Baltimore County owns 39 of the mall's 88 acres, including the Macy's parcel bought in January 2025, and is seeking developers. That is a real relocation risk for those tenants, and also a reasonable 'your customers should follow your brand' pitch.

(6) The Venue Vault's ZIP (21207) is inferred: listings omit it, and the adjacent 6325 Windsor Mill Rd is listed as 21207.

(7) Owner names are included only where the business publishes them itself: Corinthian's own site, The Reserve's own booking forms, and the Class Act business name.

(8) The best demo targets are the top three, which are event and catering businesses. Each lead is worth $1k-$10k, and each has a clearly broken or missing booking flow.
